classification.difficultyReason: Identify the useful triangle pair in the supplied auxiliary construction, justify ordered angle correspondence, and transform a corresponding-side ratio into the requested product identity.

content.prompt:
Let secants from a point, $M$, external to the circle cut the circle at points $A$ and $B$ and $P$ and $Q$, as shown in the diagram. Prove that $AM\times BM=PM\times QM$.

This is the proof of the theorem stated on page 410.

spec.description: Two secants from M with near points B and Q and far points A and P; dashed auxiliary chords AQ and BP.
spec.mathematics: All four named points lie on the circle; M,B,A and M,Q,P are collinear.
spec.answerVisibility: Source-supplied auxiliary chords remain visible; no tangent or proof answers added.

answer.short: $\triangle MAQ\sim\triangle MPB$, so $\dfrac{AM}{PM}=\dfrac{QM}{BM}$ and $AM\times BM=PM\times QM$.
answer.worked:
$\angle AMQ=\angle PMB$ because they are the same angle between the secants.

$\angle MAQ=\angle MPB$ because they are angles subtended by the same chord $BQ$.

Hence $\triangle MAQ\sim\triangle MPB$ (AA), with correspondence $M\leftrightarrow M$, $A\leftrightarrow P$, $Q\leftrightarrow B$.

Therefore,
$$\frac{AM}{PM}=\frac{QM}{BM}.$$
Multiplying by $PM\times BM$ gives
$$AM\times BM=PM\times QM.$$
